Exactly rounded dot products and norms

Source: R/dot.R
xsum_dot.Rd

xsum_dot() returns the correctly rounded value of the exact dot product sum(x * y), products included: each product is split into its rounded value and its exact rounding error with fma(), and both are added exactly. One rounding.

Usage

xsum_dot(x, y)

xsum_sqnorm(x)

xsum_norm(x)

Arguments

x, y

Numeric or logical vectors of the same length.

Value

A double of length one.

Details

xsum_sqnorm() is xsum_dot(x, x), the exactly rounded squared Euclidean norm. xsum_norm() is its square root, so it has two roundings: the squared norm and the square root.

Limits

The product error is exact only while each product is above about 2^-970 in magnitude (about 1e-292). Below that, the low bits of the error are lost to underflow, so a dot product made only of such tiny products can be off in its last bits. A product whose magnitude exceeds the largest double is Inf even if the exact dot product would be finite.

Special values

Any NA in x or y gives NA. Otherwise a NaN product (a NaN input, or 0 * Inf) gives NaN; infinite products of both signs give NaN; infinite products of one sign give that infinity.

Examples

# (1e8 + 1) * (1e8 - 1) is 1e16 - 1, which rounds to 1e16 as a double.
x <- c(1e8 + 1, 1)
y <- c(1e8 - 1, -1e16)
sum(x * y)
#> [1] 0
xsum_dot(x, y)
#> [1] -1

xsum_norm(c(3, 4))
#> [1] 5
